limited contact with irritants to minimum

concepts.why: The patient has positive reactions to multiple contact allergens, including Nickel, Cobalt, and Sesquiterpene lactone mix, which is consistent with Allergic Contact Dermatitis.
The patient has a long history of severe hand eczema, asthma, rhinitis, and a positive family history for atopy, which are all consistent with Atopic Dermatitis.
Although the patient has limited contact with irritants, the possibility of Irritant Contact Dermatitis cannot be entirely ruled out, especially given the severity of the hand eczema.
The patient has a long history of severe hand eczema, with a high HECSI score, which is consistent with Chronic Hand Eczema.
